07abc1cc-5794-51a6-bad4-40565eae52be.title: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

e-4697.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
e-4697.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
e-4697.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -8 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y=0 \\ y=1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+2(1)=0 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\left<  -2,1 \right>.$

e-4698.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
e-4698.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+5y=5 \\ x-6y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
e-4698.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & -1 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5y=-5 \\ y=-10,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-10$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-5(-10)=-5 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-55.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-55$ and $y=-10.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -55,-10 \rangle.$

M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 10 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

a
M∼[1−2−40113], x=−53 and y=13
b
M∼[1−210301−53], x=0 and y=−53
c
M∼[12401−3], x=0 and y=53
d
M∼[1−21030153], x=203 and y=53
e
M∼[1−210301−3], x=−83 and y=−3
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R1 ← R1/3 to obtain [1, -2 | 10/3]. Then R2 ← R2 − 2R1 gives [0, 1 | -5/3]. Thus y = -5/3, and back substitution into x − 2y = 10/3 gives x = 0. The correct choice is b.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 10 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 10 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & \frac{10}{3} \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & \frac{10}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=\frac{10}{3} \\  & y=-\frac{5}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-\frac{5}{3}$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-\frac{5}{3})=\frac{10}{3}\,⇒\,x=\frac{10}{3}-\frac{10}{3}=0.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=0$ and $y=-\frac{5}{3}.$

a
M∼[1−2−40113], x=−53 and y=13
b
M∼[1−210301−53], x=0 and y=−53
c
M∼[12401−3], x=0 and y=53
d
M∼[1−21030153], x=203 and y=53
e
M∼[1−210301−3], x=−83 and y=−3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[3−6102−35]R1:=13R1∼[1−21032−35]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[1−210301−53]. The system is now
{x−2y=103y=−53,

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation y=−53 tells us the value of y. Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

x−2(−53)=103⇒x=103−103=0.

Thus, the solution is x=0 and y=−53.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 10 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 10 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & \frac{10}{3} \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & \frac{10}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=\frac{10}{3} \\  & y=-\frac{5}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-\frac{5}{3}$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-\frac{5}{3})=\frac{10}{3}\,⇒\,x=\frac{10}{3}-\frac{10}{3}=0.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=0$ and $y=-\frac{5}{3}.$

Question 2
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[3−2464−8]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form.

a
M∼[10001−2]
b
M∼[1−2343012]
c
M∼[1−234301−2]
d
M∼[1−434301−1]
e
M∼[1−434301−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Scale R1 by 1/3 to obtain [1, -2/3 | 4/3]. Subtract 6R1 from R2 to obtain [0, 8 | -16], then divide R2 by 8 to obtain [0, 1 | -2]. This is the row echelon form in option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 8 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 6 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 8 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 3
before.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].

decision.explanation: Apply R2 ← R2 + R1 to obtain [0, -1 | 11], then R2 ← -R2 to obtain [0, 1 | -11]. Thus y = -11. Back substitution into x + y = 8 gives x = 19, matching option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y=8 \\  & y=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-11$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-11)=8\,⇒\,x=8+11=19.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=19$ and $y=-11.$

a

b
M∼[1180111], x=10 and y=11

M∼[1180113], x=11 and y=13
d
M∼[11801−11], x=19 and y=−11
e
M∼[11801−16], x=17 and y=−16
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[118−1−23]R2:=R2+1⋅R1∼[1180−111]R2:=−1⋅R2∼[11801−11].

The system is now
{x+y=8y=−11, and we can apply back substitution. The final equation y=−11 tells us the value of y. Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

x+(−11)=8⇒x=8+11=19.

Therefore, the solution is x=19 and y=−11.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y=8 \\  & y=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-11$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-11)=8\,⇒\,x=8+11=19.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=19$ and $y=-11.$

decision.explanation: Apply R1 ← R1/2 to obtain [1, -4 | 3]. Then R2 ← R2 − 3R1 gives [0, 5 | -5]. Dividing R2 by 5 gives [0, 1 | -1], matching option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Divide R1 by 2 to obtain [1, 3/2 | 7/2]. Then R2 ← R2 − 3R1 gives [0, -13/2 | -13/2]. Multiply R2 by -2/13 to obtain [0, 1 | 1], matching option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 7 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 7 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{7}{2} \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{7}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{13}{2} & -\frac{13}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{13}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{7}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 7 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 7 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{7}{2} \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{7}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{13}{2} & -\frac{13}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{13}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{7}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 6
before.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+5y=-6 \\  & -6x-6y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.

before.html:
Question 6
?

Consider the system of linear equations {3x+5y=−6−6x−6y=10. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[15−201−1]
b
M∼[13−201−2]
c
M∼[15320112]
d
M∼[153−201−12]
e
M∼[153−10112]
Submit

decision.explanation: The augmented matrix has rows [3, 5 | -6] and [-6, -6 | 10]. Divide R1 by 3 to obtain [1, 5/3 | -2]. Then R2 ← R2 + 6R1 gives [0, 4 | -2]. Divide R2 by 4 to obtain [0, 1 | -1/2], matching option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+5y=-6 \\  & -6x-6y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -6 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -6 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ 0 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+5y=-6 \\  & -6x-6y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -6 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -6 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ -6 & -6 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ 0 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{3} & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Consider the system of linear equations {x−3y=−82x+4y=4. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
M∼[1−3−8015], x=−2 and y=2
b
M∼[10−8012], x=−8 and y=2
c
M∼[1−3−8012], x=−2 and y=2
d
M∼[1−3−8011], x=−4 and y=1
e
M∼[1−3−801−2], x=−4 and y=1
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R2 ← R2 − 2R1 to obtain [0, 10 | 20], then divide R2 by 10 to obtain [0, 1 | 2]. Thus y = 2, and x − 3(2) = −8 gives x = −2. This matches option c.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-8 \\  & 2x+4y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 10 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-8 \\  & y=2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(2)=-8\,⇒\,x=-2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=2.$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-8 \\  & 2x+4y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 10 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=-8 \\  & y=2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(2)=-8\,⇒\,x=-2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=2.$

x−3(2)=−8⇒x=−2.

Therefore, the solution is x=−2 and y=2.

before.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-2y=4 \\  & 2x-y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.

Consider the system of linear equations {3x−2y=42x−y=2. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[1−23430132]
b
M∼[1−234301−32]
c
M∼[1−234301−3]
d
M∼[1−2343012]
e

decision.explanation: Divide R1 by 3 to obtain [1, -2/3 | 4/3]. Then R2 ← R2 − 2R1 gives [0, 1/3 | -2/3]. Multiplying R2 by 3 gives [0, 1 | -2], matching option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-2y=4 \\  & 2x-y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-2y=4 \\  & 2x-y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Consider the system of linear equations {2x+7y=−57x+11y=−4. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[172−52011]
b
M∼[17−501−2]
c
M∼[17−5010]
d
M∼[172−5201−3]
e
M∼[172−5201−1]
Submit

decision.explanation: Divide R1 by 2 to obtain [1, 7/2 | -5/2]. Then R2 ← R2 − 7R1 gives [0, -27/2 | 27/2]. Multiplying R2 by -2/27 gives [0, 1 | -1], matching option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+7y=-5 \\  & 7x+11y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -5 \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -5 \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{27}{2} & \frac{27}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{27}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+7y=-5 \\  & 7x+11y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -5 \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -5 \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 7 & 11 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{27}{2} & \frac{27}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{27}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations {4x+12y=−45x+11y=3. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[13−1012]
b
M∼[13−101−2]
c
M∼[13−101−4]
d
M∼[13−101−1]
e
M∼[13−1011]
Submit

decision.explanation: Divide R1 by 4 to obtain [1, 3 | -1]. Then R2 ← R2 − 5R1 gives [0, -4 | 8]. Dividing R2 by -4 gives [0, 1 | -2], matching option b.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 4x+12y=-4 \\  & 5x+11y=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 12 & -4 \\ 5 & 11 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 12 & -4 \\ 5 & 11 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 5 & 11 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 4x+12y=-4 \\  & 5x+11y=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 12 & -4 \\ 5 & 11 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 12 & -4 \\ 5 & 11 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 5 & 11 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
